threats.title: Session fixation, theft, or excessive persistence

controls.decision: Use a same-origin confidential BFF with server-held tokens by default.
verification: BFF browser storage contains no OAuth tokens
browser refresh resumes only through the server session

controls.decision: Use Authorization Code with PKCE S256 and exact redirect validation; never use implicit or password grants.
verification: real-provider login succeeds through code flow

controls.decision: Give the BFF browser only an opaque protected Secure HttpOnly host cookie and retain tickets server-side.
verification: cookie flags and host scope are asserted
cookie payload is not a bearer or refresh token

controls.decision: Require antiforgery validation for unsafe cookie-authenticated API and logout requests.
verification: missing and invalid antiforgery tokens fail

controls.decision: Validate issuer, audience, signature, lifetime, state, nonce, local return paths, and normalize provider claims into canonical application permissions.
verification: invalid identity and unmapped provider inputs grant no permissions

controls.decision: Require authentication by fallback and enforce named authorization policies at protected server endpoints.
Terminate the local RP session before best-effort provider logout and do not claim back-channel logout without full logout-token validation.
verification: provider outage cannot restore local session
unverified logout callbacks are not accepted

controls.decision: Apply documented idle and non-extendable absolute session bounds controlled by the RP.
Disable CORS for BFF and use exact allowlisted origins for direct SPA API access.
verification: wildcard credentials are rejected at startup

controls.decision: Apply restrictive content, framing, referrer, permission, MIME, and transport browser policies.
Bound app-controlled identity operations and expose redacted fixed-shape health and errors.
verification: health and errors contain no provider internals or secrets

controls.decision: Pin identity fixtures and test dependencies, exclude generated authentication state, and execute real-provider negative journeys.
verification: pinned assets and lock files are present

controls.decision: Reject incomplete or contradictory profile configuration at startup and governance gates.
verification: invalid settings fail startup with path-specific errors
architecture readiness requires the exact profile and assurance IDs

configurableDefaults.rationale: Leaves time inside the five-second app-controlled outcome budget for deterministic failure handling.
configurableDefaults.overrideWhen: Measured local or deployed discovery latency cannot meet the budget without false degradation.
configurableDefaults.requiredEvidence: Latency distribution, chosen service objective, bounded-failure test, and owner approval.

configurableDefaults.rationale: Provides a deterministic user-visible upper bound for operations still controlled by the application.
configurableDefaults.overrideWhen: A measured product service objective or dependency budget requires another value.
configurableDefaults.requiredEvidence: Approved SLO, dependency budget, user-impact analysis, and outage test.

configurableDefaults.rationale: Bounds server-controlled protocol work without pretending to bound time spent on an external provider page.
configurableDefaults.overrideWhen: Provider measurements and the product login SLO justify a different bound.
configurableDefaults.requiredEvidence: Provider latency evidence, login SLO, failure UX, and regression test.

configurableDefaults.rationale: Limits unattended-session exposure while remaining usable for ordinary business interaction.
configurableDefaults.overrideWhen: The application assurance level, device posture, data sensitivity, or workflow duration differs.
configurableDefaults.requiredEvidence: AAL/risk assessment, user-impact analysis, privacy review where monitoring is added, and expiry tests.

configurableDefaults.rationale: Provides a non-extendable working-day bound for RP and refresh-token use.
configurableDefaults.overrideWhen: The application risk assessment requires shorter, longer, or step-up-authenticated sessions.
configurableDefaults.requiredEvidence: AAL/risk assessment, refresh-token policy, reauthentication design, and absolute-expiry test.

configurableDefaults.rationale: Creates deterministic fallback and representative localization test coverage; it is not a security claim.
configurableDefaults.requiredEvidence: Product locale decision and fallback/missing-key tests.

configurableDefaults.setting: local ports, origins, client IDs, personas, and Keycloak fixture
configurableDefaults.rationale: Makes the inherited boundary executable and repeatable without claiming production suitability.
configurableDefaults.overrideWhen: Deployment topology, provider, ownership, or collision constraints differ.
configurableDefaults.requiredEvidence: Exact deployment configuration, secret/origin review, provider contract tests, and non-production credential isolation.

configurableDefaults.rationale: Provides a restrictive starting point but cannot anticipate every frontend resource and rendering decision.
configurableDefaults.overrideWhen: A required resource or framework capability is blocked.
configurableDefaults.requiredEvidence: Minimal directive change, threat review, browser assertion, and no broad unsafe fallback without explicit risk acceptance.

residualRisks.risk: BFF prevents browser token extraction but same-origin malicious code can still issue actions through the victim session.
residualRisks.treatment: Prevent XSS, restrict dependencies and CSP, enforce business authorization, and monitor sensitive actions.

residualRisks.risk: RP-initiated logout cannot guarantee termination of an unavailable provider or every other relying-party session.
residualRisks.treatment: Guarantee local termination; add standards-compliant back-channel logout only with verified tokens and session correlation.

residualRisks.risk: A compromised identity provider, host, key store, reverse proxy, or deployment control plane defeats assumptions of the profile.
residualRisks.treatment: Apply provider, host, key, secret, network, supply-chain, monitoring, and incident-response controls outside this profile.

residualRisks.risk: The SPA profile exposes bearer-token consequences to malicious browser code.
residualRisks.treatment: Prefer BFF; otherwise document necessity, keep tokens memory-only, minimize lifetime/scope, harden content, and test leakage.

required: Playwright against the pinned Keycloak fixture
refresh, logout, outage, storage, and header assertions

reviewTriggers.trigger: RFC, OpenID, NIST, browser-platform, or ASP.NET security guidance materially changes or the browser-app draft becomes final.
reviewTriggers.action: Re-evaluate affected controls, defaults, residual risks, tests, and profile compatibility.

reviewTriggers.trigger: A profile, OAuth/OIDC library, runtime major version, identity provider, token-storage model, cookie model, or deployment topology changes.
reviewTriggers.action: Perform architecture and migration review before adoption.

reviewTriggers.trigger: A relevant vulnerability, incident, penetration-test finding, conformance failure, or dependency advisory is reported.
reviewTriggers.action: Reassess threat likelihood and control sufficiency immediately; patch or revoke affected evidence.

reviewTriggers.trigger: A consuming project overrides a security-sensitive default or accepts a listed residual risk.
reviewTriggers.action: Record owner, rationale, evidence, expiry/review condition, and regression coverage in an Accepted ADR.

reviewTriggers.trigger: Twelve months pass since last review even if no other trigger is known.
reviewTriggers.action: Verify source currency, implementation behavior, dependency state, and claim wording; update lastReviewed.
